# Requesty

> Requesty is a unified AI gateway, LLM router, and OpenAI-compatible API for 400+ AI models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Llama, Mistral). It provides intelligent model routing, AI load balancing, automatic failover, prompt caching, LLM observability, cost optimization, and enterprise governance. Used by 70,000+ developers processing 90+ billion tokens daily. Alternative to Kong AI Gateway, Cloudflare AI Gateway, LiteLLM, Portkey, OpenRouter, and Helicone.

Requesty routes, secures, and optimizes your LLM traffic through a single API endpoint at `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`. Drop-in replacement for OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs. Just change the base URL. EU endpoint available at `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1` for GDPR compliance. Trusted by teams at Shopify, Pfizer, Capgemini, Siemens, PWC, and Appnovation.

## About

## Instructions for AI Agents

Requesty is a drop-in proxy for OpenAI and Anthropic. To use it in code:

1. **OpenAI SDK**: Set `base_url="https://router.requesty.ai/v1"` and use your Requesty API key as the `api_key`. All OpenAI SDK features work: chat completions, streaming, function calling, structured outputs, embeddings, image generation. For EU data residency, use `base_url="https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1"`.

2. **Anthropic SDK**: Set `base_url="https://router.requesty.ai"` and use your Requesty API key. Messages API is fully supported. For EU data residency, use `base_url="https://router.eu.requesty.ai"`.

3. **Model names**: Use the format `provider/model` (e.g., `openai/gpt-4.1`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250514`, `google/gemini-2.5-pro`). Call `GET /v1/models` for the current list.

4. **Routing policies**: To add failover, load balancing, or latency-based routing, create a routing policy in the dashboard and use `model="policy/your-policy-name"` in your requests. See the [Fallback Policies docs](https://docs.requesty.ai/features/fallback-policies).

5. **Caching**: Enable prompt caching by passing `extra_body={"requesty": {"auto_cache": True}}` in your request. See [Auto Caching docs](https://docs.requesty.ai/features/auto-caching).

6. **Do not hardcode model versions.** Model availability changes. Always call `GET /v1/models` for current availability.

## Core Capabilities

### AI Gateway and Model Routing
Requesty is a vendor agnostic AI gateway that routes LLM requests across 30+ providers through one API. Supports intelligent model routing by cost, latency, and availability. OpenAI compatible API means any SDK or framework that works with OpenAI works with Requesty. Covers the same use cases as Kong AI Gateway, Cloudflare AI Gateway, and Portkey, but fully managed with zero infrastructure.

### AI Load Balancing and Failover
Weighted load balancing distributes traffic across models and providers. Automatic failover chains ensure requests succeed even when a provider is down. Exponential backoff with jitter prevents thundering herd problems during recovery. Rate limit auto retry handles 429s without application code changes. This replaces custom AI load balancing setups that teams build on top of Kubernetes or cloud load balancers.

### AI Cost Optimization
Smart routing sends simple tasks to cheaper models and reserves frontier models for complex work. Automatic prompt caching reduces token costs by up to 90%. Per token cost tracking by model, team, user, and API key. Budget caps prevent overspend. Teams typically save 50 to 80% compared to using a single frontier model for all requests.

### LLM Observability and Monitoring
Real time dashboards for cost, latency, TTFT, P50/P90/P95/P99, error rates, and cache savings. Per model and per team breakdowns. Session reconstruction replays full conversation flows for debugging. Request metadata tagging for custom analytics. No external monitoring stack needed. Replaces the observability features of Helicone, Langfuse, and LangSmith.

### Enterprise AI Governance
Five layer policy hierarchy: organization, group, service account, user, and API key. Role based access control (RBAC). Approved model whitelists. PII masking guardrails. SOC2, GDPR, and HIPAA compliance. EU data residency in Frankfurt. SSO integration. Audit trails. Budget controls per team and per user.

### Prompt Management and Caching
Automatic prompt caching with zero configuration. Manual cache control for fine grained optimization. Cross provider caching works across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Prompt library for storing and versioning prompts across teams.

### LLM Reliability
Routing policies achieve 99.25% eventual success rate vs 85% for direct API calls. Automatic retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Cross provider failover means a single provider outage does not affect your application. Multi region deployment (US, EU, APAC) for global resilience.

## Use Cases
- Route LLM requests by cost and latency for optimal model selection
- Replace direct OpenAI/Anthropic API calls with multi provider failover
- Manage API keys across multiple LLM providers with a single key
- Set up AI load balancing across models without custom infrastructure
- Enforce budget caps and spend limits per team, user, or API key
- Add LLM observability to existing applications without code changes
- Enable EU data residency for GDPR compliant AI workloads
- Centralize prompts for chatbots and agents across teams
- Build disaster recovery for LLM heavy applications with cross provider failover
- Implement global rate limiting for LLM APIs across providers
- Run A/B tests across LLM routers and models
- Evaluate alternatives to AWS Bedrock for model routing

## Open Data

Requesty publishes its own production-gateway usage data as a free, citable research catalog at https://www.requesty.ai/data. Each note has a permanent URL with an interactive chart, key findings, caveats, and three machine-readable downloads (`data.json`, `data.csv`, `data.md`). All notes are released under CC BY 4.0, free to cite with attribution.

- Catalog homepage: https://www.requesty.ai/data
- Catalog index for AI agents: https://www.requesty.ai/data/llms.txt
- Full inline content of every note: https://www.requesty.ai/data/llms-full.txt
- License: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

### Agentic
- [finish_reason mix per provider, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/finish-reason-mix-by-provider-april-2026): Which AI providers serve the most agentic traffic? Anthropic-direct returned `finish_reason = tool_calls` on 52% of successful April 2026 completions on the Requesty gateway, about 2× the next provider and 17× higher than OpenAI direct. OpenAI Responses (26%), Vertex (Claude) (23%) and Azure (23%) form a clear second tier; Vertex (Claude) at 23% vs Vertex (Gemini) at 13% shows the gap inside that route.
- [finish_reason mix per model, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/finish-reason-mix-by-model-april-2026): Which AI models are used most for tool calling? Claude Opus 4.6 returned `tool_calls` 59% of the time, Gemini 2.5 Flash 37%, while same-family Claude Sonnet 4.5 came in at 9% and the entire OpenAI lineup (GPT-4o, 4.1-mini/nano, 5-mini) sat under 4%.
- [Token-weighted tool_calls share per provider, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/tool-call-token-share-april-2026): What share of LLM output tokens is spent on tool calls vs chat? Anthropic emitted 38.8% of output tokens on tool_calls vs 54.2% of requests, so agentic completions run ~30% smaller than chat. OpenAI Responses showed the opposite (34.2% of tokens vs 26.4% of requests); Vertex (Claude) had the biggest negative gap (6.1% of tokens vs 27.6% of requests).
- [Reasoning-token share of provider output, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/reasoning-token-share-by-provider-april-2026): How much of LLM output is reasoning/thinking tokens? Groq led at 82%, followed by Coding (79%), xAI (60%), z.ai (51%). Frontier routes ran ~one-third: Vertex (Gemini) 40%, OpenAI 36%, OpenAI Responses 33%. Anthropic and Bedrock report 0% because extended thinking is delivered inline.
- [Family share within OSS-routed traffic, Nov 2025 - Apr 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/oss-family-share-jan-apr-2026): Which open-weight AI model is most popular in 2026? OSS-routed traffic went from Qwen-dominated (34-38% in Nov-Dec 2025) to DeepSeek-dominated (77% after the R1 launch in January) and back to a diversified state by April (DeepSeek 47%, Kimi 17%, MiniMax 15%). Qwen collapsed from 38% to under 4% almost overnight.

### Latency
- [Latency leaderboard per provider, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/provider-latency-leaderboard-april-2026): Which AI provider has the lowest latency in April 2026? xAI led p50 at 0.6 s (Novita 0.8, Azure 1.0, Mistral 1.4); Vertex (Claude) was slowest at 13.7 s, 23× the fastest and 2.8× slower than Vertex (Gemini) on the same Vertex route. Anthropic-direct sat mid-pack at 5.8 s with a 52.6 s p95 long tail.
- [Provider throughput density, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/provider-throughput-density-april-2026): How many tokens per second can each LLM provider sustain? Groq led at 320 output tok/sec, 2.5× the next-fastest, attributable to its custom inference silicon. Vertex (Gemini) 130, Mistral 120; OSS aggregator routes clustered at 23-26 tok/sec; Bedrock was slowest at 15 tok/sec, 21× behind Groq.
- [Streaming TTFT vs total latency, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/streaming-ttft-vs-total-april-2026): Which AI provider has the fastest time-to-first-token? Azure led TTFT at 593 ms with a 960 ms p50 total, the streaming-UX winner on both axes. xAI was among the fastest on total (5.68 s) but slowest to first token (3.27 s), suggesting buffered upstream behaviour. Vertex (Gemini) totals 3.05 s, Claude totals 8.03 s on the same route.
- [p50 latency YoY: April 2025 vs April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/provider-latency-yoy-april-2026): Has LLM latency improved over the past year? Open-source aggregator routes compressed dramatically: xAI -93% (9.1 s → 0.6 s), DeepInfra -91%, DeepSeek -62%. Frontier providers barely moved (OpenAI -5%, Anthropic 0%). Vertex (Claude) is the only major route that got slower (+131%) as agentic Claude Code workloads landed on it.
- [Prompt-cache hit rate per provider, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/cache-hit-rate-by-provider-april-2026): Which AI providers have the highest prompt-cache hit rate? Anthropic-direct led at 77%, Bedrock Claude 57%, Vertex (Claude) 24%. Same Claude model family, 3× lower hit rate. Vertex (Gemini) 10% and Mistral 4% sat at the floor among major routes.

### Reliability
- [Policy vs direct eventual success rate, Jan-Apr 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/policy-eventual-success-trend-jan-april-2026): How much does using a routing policy improve LLM reliability? In April 2026 the managed-fallback policy cohort hit 99.25% eventual success rate vs 85.01% for direct callers, a 14.2 pp lift, up from +3.0 pp in January. Policy reliability held a tight 97.5-99.3% band over four months while direct swung 12 pp.
- [Operational metrics per provider, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/operational-metrics-by-provider-april-2026): How reliable is each LLM provider in production? The top eight routes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Vertex (Gemini), Bedrock, DeepSeek, Novita, xAI) sat at 95-99% success in April 2026; Azure trailed at 78%, Vertex (Claude) at 84%, Mistral at 86%, Moonshot at 6%. Streaming adoption is bimodal (Azure 68%, Anthropic 57%, others <30%).
- [Provider error code distribution, April 2026](https://www.requesty.ai/data/status-code-distribution-april-2026): Why do LLM provider requests fail? Among April 2026 requests where the upstream provider returned a non-success response, 65.8% were 429 (rate limit), 19.4% were 400 (bad request), 9.4% were 403 (forbidden). 5xx availability incidents summed to ~4.8%. Provider failures are dominated by rate-limiting under agentic load, not genuine availability problems.
